ops.insert: Objective: Develop the FairFright website and app with automated and active processes.
A secure sign-up and login system for all user types.
The user interface and available features dynamically adapt based on whether the user is a shipper, transporter, or admin.
A critical security and quality feature where new transporters must be manually approved by an admin before they can access the marketplace, ensuring a high-quality network.
A professional, modern landing page that serves as the "front door" to the application, effectively communicating FairFreight's value proposition to new visitors.
All users can manage their personal and organizational profiles, including updating contact details and company logos.
Shipper Features ("I have goods to move")
Provides shippers with a quick overview of their key logistics metrics, including total spend and number of jobs posted.
Shippers can quickly post immediate freight needs (both Full Truckload and Less-Than-Truckload) to the open market for transporters to bid on.
When posting a load, an AI-powered tool analyzes the freight details and suggests the most appropriate truck type.
For long-term needs, shippers can create detailed Requests for Proposals (RFPs), invite specific transporters to bid, review submissions, and award multi-year contracts.
A centralized view to track the status of all posted jobs, compare incoming bids, and award jobs to their chosen transporter.
A dedicated section to view all completed jobs and manage their payment status.
After a job is completed, shippers can rate the transporter and leave a review, which contributes to the transporter's public-facing average rating.
Transporter Features ("I have trucks to fill")
Gives transporters a snapshot of their business performance, including total earnings, jobs completed, and their average shipper rating.
A real-time view of all available loads on the market, with powerful filtering and searching capabilities to find the right jobs.
A simple and intuitive interface to place competitive bids on available loads.
Once a job is won, transporters can update its status through the entire lifecycle, from "En Route to Pickup" all the way to "Delivered".
An integrated tool that provides AI-driven route suggestions for active jobs, helping transporters save time and fuel by considering traffic and historical data.
A dedicated section for transporters to add and manage the vehicles in their fleet.
Transporters can plan multi-stop trips and consolidate Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) shipments from the marketplace onto a single truck, maximizing efficiency and profitability.
A high-level dashboard that shows key metrics for the entire platform, such as total jobs created, gross marketplace value (GMV), and user counts.
A tool for admins to review and approve or reject pending transporter applications, ensuring the quality and integrity of the transporter network.
Admins can view and monitor all jobs currently active on the platform.

Sprint 1: Project Scaffolding, Branding & Firebase Setup #planning
Initialize the Turborepo monorepo with web, mobile, firebase, and ui packages
Set up the new Firebase project in the console (Auth, Firestore, Storage)
Create and configure .env files for Firebase API keys in both web and mobile apps
Create the Firebase client initialization file (/firebase/client.ts) (Web App)
Create the Firebase client initialization file (/firebase/client.ts) (Mobile App)
Create and export the shared Header.tsx component
Install and configure Tailwind CSS (Web App)
Add the FairFreight color palette to tailwind.config.ts and set the global background color (Web App)
Create the shared theme.ts file under a packages/config directory
Initialize the firebase folder for Cloud Functions with the Firebase CLI
Write the initial, baseline Firestore Security Rules (must be authenticated to R/W)
Build the /auth page UI with sign-up and login forms styled with the FairFreight theme (Web App)
Build the Auth screens (Sign Up, Login) using FairFreight styles (Mobile App)
Implement the sign-up logic (Firebase Auth + Firestore batched write for user & organization creation) (Web App)
Implement the same sign-up and login logic as the web app (for transporters) (Mobile App)
Set up React Navigation with a protected stack group for the main app content (Mobile App)
Create a protected route HOC or middleware to redirect unauthenticated users (Web App)
Create the multi-step Onboarding screen flow (Mobile App)
Build the UI forms to collect company and vehicle details (Mobile App)
Implement document upload functionality using expo-image-picker and Firebase Storage (Mobile App)
Create the admin-only /admin/vetting page UI (Web App)
Implement the Firestore query to fetch all organizations with vettingStatus: 'pending' (Web App)
Add 'View Documents' links and an 'Approve' button to each entry in the table (Web App)
Write and deploy the approveTransporter callable Cloud Function (Backend)
Update Firestore Security Rules to protect document uploads and the admin area (Backend)
Sprint 4: Shipper Experience - Posting & Monitoring Jobs #development
Build the /jobs/new page and the CreateJobForm.tsx component (Web App)
Integrate Google Places API for address autocomplete (Web App)
Implement the logic to write a new job document to Firestore on form submission (Web App)
Build the dynamic /jobs/[jobId] page UI to display job details (Web App)
Implement the real-time listener on the bids sub-collection and display the results (Web App)
Refine security rules for the jobs collection (Backend)
Sprint 5: Transporter Experience - Finding & Bidding on Jobs #development
Build the 'Find Jobs' screen UI (Mobile App)
Implement the real-time Firestore query to fetch jobs where status === 'bidding' (Mobile App)
Build the JobDetails screen UI (Mobile App)
Write security rules to ensure only approved transporters can see jobs and place bids (Backend)
Implement the logic to write a new bid document to the /jobs/{jobId}/bids sub-collection (Mobile App)
Build the bidding modal UI (Mobile App)
Sprint 6: Closing the Loop - Job Awarding & Execution #development
Add the 'Accept Bid' button to the bids list on the /jobs/[jobId] page (Web App)
Link the 'Accept Bid' button to trigger the awardJob Cloud Function (Web App)
Write and deploy the transactional awardJob Cloud Function (Backend)
Build the 'My Jobs' screen, showing awarded jobs (Mobile App)
Build the LiveJob management screen UI with its context-aware status button (Mobile App)
Implement the Firestore updates for each status change (Mobile App)
Implement the final 'Upload POD' functionality (Mobile App)
Build the generic chat components (ChatWindow, MessageBubble, ChatInput) (Shared UI)
Integrate the chat components into the LiveJob screen (Mobile App)
Integrate the chat components into the /jobs/[jobId] page, visible only after a job is awarded (Web App)
Define and secure the chats collection and messages sub-collection (Backend)
Configure Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) and get APN/FCM keys (DevOps/Infra)
Add logic to request notification permissions and save the FCM token to the user's Firestore document (Mobile App)
Modify the awardJob function to send notifications to the winner and losers (Backend)
Create a function that triggers on new messages in the chat collection to notify the recipient (Backend)
(Optional) Create a function that notifies transporters of new relevant jobs (Backend)
Review and finalize all Firestore Security Rules for production (DevOps/Infra)
Document and fix any bugs found (QA/Testing)
Perform comprehensive end-to-end testing of the entire core loop with multiple test accounts (QA/Testing)
Choose and integrate an analytics provider (e.g., Mixpanel, PostHog, or Google Analytics) (Analytics)
Add event tracking for key user actions: user_signup, job_created, bid_placed, job_awarded, pod_uploaded (Analytics)
Create a production build and set up hosting (Vercel is ideal) (Web App)
Use Expo Application Services (EAS) to build the standalone app binaries (.apk/.ipa) (Mobile App)
Prepare App Store and Google Play Store listings (Mobile App)
Ensure all Firebase plans are upgraded to a paid plan (Blaze) for launch (DevOps/Infra)
